mode.condition: Non-64-bit x86 with default 32-bit operand and address sizes, consistent with the verified program language x86:LE:32:default.

physical.opcode_group: Group 1 arithmetic/logical r/m32 with sign-extended imm8

modrm.interpretation: mod=00 and r/m=101 select an absolute disp32 memory offset under 32-bit address size; /4 selects AND.

operands.linear_address: DS.base plus effective offset under the assumed 32-bit execution model; DS.base is unqueried.

physical.operation_on_normal_completion: old = read32(DS:0109EEA8); result = old AND sign_extend32(imm8 00) = 00000000; write32(DS:0109EEA8, result).

flags_on_normal_completion.derivation: AND clears CF and OF; SF/ZF/PF follow the 32-bit result, which is zero. Its low byte has even parity.

fault_and_execution_conditions: Saved Ghidra bytes and program language do not establish that this instruction executes, is fetchable, or is reachable in the live process.

The memory operand is a read-modify-write even with a zero immediate. Successful execution requires the relevant segment and page accesses, including write permission; it is not evidence that the memory is present or writable.
Under protected 32-bit execution, invalid/null DS selection, unsuitable segment access rights, or a four-byte operand outside the segment limit can cause #GP. No DS descriptor or limit was queried.
Instruction fetch or the memory access can encounter paging faults according to the actual paging state. No page tables, memory contents, allocation identity, or device-memory behavior was queried.

The encoded offset 0109EEA8 is four-byte aligned. Alignment-check #AC depends on the resulting linear address and active alignment-check/privilege controls; the unknown DS base prevents an unconditional live alignment claim.
The zero memory result, flag values and next EIP apply only on normal completion. This record does not model fault delivery, handlers, interrupts, debug traps, or memory-mapped-device side effects.
No LOCK prefix is present. The instruction does not establish an atomic read-modify-write operation relative to other processors or agents.

accepted_lineage.additional_mapping_qualification: Saved listing addresses are not automatically CPU EIP offsets. Any future CALL/RET or sequential EIP interpretation must explicitly condition the mapping, for example that listing addresses correspond to runtime linear addresses and CS.base is zero. That mapping and CS.base remain unverified; no context query is authorized.

ordinary_near_return_semantics.condition: The stated 32-bit operand-size decode and normal completion in the ordinary near-return model.
ordinary_near_return_semantics.SS_B_1: Read the four-byte little-endian return offset from SS:ESP, advance ESP by four modulo 2^32, and load that return offset into EIP after applicable checks.
ordinary_near_return_semantics.SS_B_0: Use SS:SP as the stack address and advance SP by four modulo 2^16. The popped return offset remains four bytes because operand size is 32 bits; the upper ESP bits are not thereby a proven full-ESP-plus-four update.
ordinary_near_return_semantics.EIP_value: The unqueried popped CPU return offset, not an authenticated listing address.
ordinary_near_return_semantics.linear_destination: Current CS.base plus the popped return offset under the assumed execution model, subject to architectural checks; neither value was observed.
ordinary_near_return_semantics.EFLAGS: Unchanged by the ordinary RET opcode semantics.
ordinary_near_return_semantics.additional_enabled_control_protection_fe: Their state was not queried. The ordinary model does not establish absence of shadow-stack or other protection checks or their extra effects.

fault_and_execution_conditions: The saved byte and program language do not establish reachability, fetchability, actual CPU mode or execution of this RET.

The four-byte return-slot read must satisfy the active stack segment and paging rules. Stack bounds or access can fault, including #SS under applicable protected-mode conditions, and the memory read can encounter #PF.
A popped return offset outside the applicable code-segment limit can produce #GP rather than normal completion. The CS descriptor, limit and popped value are unqueried.
An unaligned stack read can incur #AC when the applicable privilege and alignment-check controls enable it. Actual stack address, SS base and those controls are unqueried.
Continuation at the resulting target also depends on instruction-fetch permissions and mapping; a destination fetch fault is not evidence of a decoded sequential successor.
If additional control-protection facilities are enabled, further checks or faults may apply; the captured byte alone does not establish that configuration.
Stack-pointer, EIP and unchanged-flag statements are conditional normal-completion semantics, not a prediction of exception delivery, handlers, interrupts, debug behavior or live runtime state.
